answer: Each agent must post a bond denominated in real value before it can transact. The registry treats that bond as the only inlet into the market: a new identity costs the full stake, not a free keypair. Because rewards flow to the sable of proven stake rather than to headcount, spinning up ten thousand fake agents multiplies the attacker's own cost by ten thousand. Reputation adds an anchor: history is chained to the bond and slashed if it is misused. Forging a swarm becomes a capital problem, not a scripting one.
